newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks in record one-day slump on rupiah.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks in record one-day slump on rupiah.

text.p: Jakarta stocks on Monday plunged more than eight percent -- their biggest intra-day drop in history -- as the weak rupiah and increased margin calls set off a selling spree, analysts said.

The composite index dived 8.41 percent, or more than 50 points, to 565.78 points, in the morning as investors panicked in the face of further weakness in the beleagured rupiah, Friday's fall on Wall Street and increased margin calls.
It later recovered slightly to close at 599.64 points, still down almost three percent and a closing low for the year. Brokers attributed the rebound to bargain hunting.
"It's not only a black Monday, it's the blackest Monday," said Hengky Sumarli, the sales director of Amantara Securities, a local brokerage house.

"The sharp drop today in Jakarta is triggered by the fall in the Dow Jones (index) on Friday combined with continued nervousness about the Indonesian rupiah movement," said Mirza Adityaswara, an analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Indonesia.
"The recent fluctuation in the rupiah had made Indonesia's risk premium become higher," he said.
He added that currency movements may prompt fund managers to review asset locations in the region, including Indonesia.

Sumarli said the plummeting sentiment was exacerbated by an increase in margin-calls. "It forced brokerage houses to liquidate their clients' positions if they were not able to inject fresh funds," he said.

The rupiah flirted with the 3,000 level against the dollar in afternoon trade, a historic low. It has fallen over 27 percent since the beginning of the year and about 25 percent since the beginning of July.
The unit was floated last weak after the central bank said it was difficult to protect it in the face of sustained overseas pressure on all regional currencies.

"The main thing is the currency and the lack of confidence," said Stephen Rogers, head of research for UBS Securities, referring to the woes afflicting the stock market. "Everything else is a contributory fact."
Brokers pointed to short-covering by local investors, high short-term interest rates and Friday's 247-point fall on the Dow Jones index as other reasons for the sell-off.
However, brokers said, the current conditions had provided an excellent buying opportunity for some stocks.
"This is a very excellent opportunity to buy back stocks which have hit rock-bottom prices," said John Rahmat, an analyst with Schroders Securities Indonesia.

He added that the weakness of the Indonesian rupiah and the high interest rates would not sustain at the current level although other brokers said any recovery would have to await some stability in the currency market.
"Investors will remain prudent. We are still waiting for further direction in the rupiah," said Vera Marpaung, a broker at Asian Development Securities.

Roland Haas, president director of Lippo Investments, said however that volumes were thin and since it was a market holiday in Hong Kong, there could be some rebound when foreigners return to the market on Tuesday.
"That's one view," he said. "But foreigners are also dependent on fund redemptions. So if their funds are seeing redemptions, they will continue selling."
